phase_1_understand_the_problem.problem_restatement: Evaluate the definite integral ∫₀^π dx/(4+3cos x) using the Weierstrass substitution t = tan(x/2).
phase_1_understand_the_problem.key_observation: The presence of cos x in the denominator suggests the universal substitution t = tan(x/2) to convert to a rational integral in t. The upper limit x = π gives t → ∞.

phase_3_plan_the_approach.strategy: Substitute t = tan(x/2), simplify 4+3cos x to (7+t²)/(1+t²), cancel (1+t²) factors, and evaluate the resulting ∫2dt/(7+t²) using the arctan formula.
logical_steps: Step 1: Substitute t = tan(x/2), write cos x and dx
Step 5: Apply arctan formula and evaluate at limits

phase_5_verify_answer.verification: After substitution the integral reduces to 2∫₀^∞ dt/(7+t²) = 2·(1/√7)·(π/2) = π/√7 ✓
